definition: Efficacious means producing the intended result, said of remedies and measures rather than of people.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word efficacious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know efficacious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Of every trick the new parents tried, only the car ride was truly efficacious — the baby was asleep before the second stoplight.
A helpful remedy does some good; an efficacious one does the specific job it was given.
Infallible goes past efficacious — not just proven to work, but claimed never to fail at all.

Effective is the everyday, all-purpose word for whatever works, and it attaches to people as happily as to pills — an effective coach, an effective policy. Efficacious is its lab-coat cousin: a formal ruling reserved for remedies and measures that have been tested against their intended result and passed.

Effectual judges actions and means — a plan, a protest, a clause — asking only whether the step actually achieved its aim. Like efficacious, it is bookish and keeps its distance from people; it fits the remedy or the maneuver, never the person applying it.

Alder Hill had eaten three budgets.
Fines slowed nobody; cameras got stolen; the rumble strips wore smooth in a year.
Then the city painted the crossing as a floating optical illusion — stripes that seem to hover a foot above the asphalt — and average speeds dropped nine miles per hour in a month.
The traffic office, burned three times, ran the numbers twice before saying it aloud: the paint was efficacious.
Efficacious is the exact word because the paint produced the intended result — effective, and proven so.
The word is a ruling, not a hope: it arrives after the trial, when the numbers are in.
That after-the-numbers flavor is why it clings to remedies, treatments, and measures rather than to people.
Efficacious is the lab-coat cousin of effective: reach for it when something has been tested against its intended result — remedies, policies, treatments — and passed.
For people, use effective or capable; "an efficacious teacher" sounds like a dosage.
And keep it clear of efficient, which measures how little a process wastes, not whether it works.

When aphids overran the community garden, the message board filled with remedies.
Members swore by crushed garlic, dish soap, marigold borders, and a chant one gardener had learned from her aunt.
Rather than argue, the plot captains ran a test: six beds, one treatment each, aphid counts posted every Friday.
By midsummer only one treatment had proved efficacious — the dish soap solution, which cut counts by ninety percent and kept them down.
The garlic did a little, the marigolds fed the rabbits, and the chant, its champion conceded, worked mainly on morale.
